# Bitpeek: Local-First Binary Workbench

> A client-only binary workbench for inspecting bytes, parsing file structures, and generating reproducible evidence reports and patches.

## Overview
- **Zero server processing**: All byte operations, hashing, parsing, and patch creation execute entirely client-side in browser memory or local process via CLI/MCP.
- **Unified Engine**: The same TypeScript core powers the web interface, the `bitpeek` CLI tool, and the local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
- **Engineered by**: Yudistira Putra (Yudis-bit).

- [Documentation Index](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs): Comprehensive technical manual for human engineers and automated agents.
- [Quickstart Guide](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs/quickstart): 3 practical tasks (hex inspect, header validation, diff patching).
- [Byte Semantics](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs/byte-semantics): Ranges, endianness, signed integer representation, IEEE-754 floats, encodings.
- [Structures Inspector](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs/structures): In-depth guide to ELF, PNG, and declarative custom schemas.
- [Patches & Diff](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs/patches): Offset-aligned diff semantics, precondition checks, and atomic verified patch apply.
- [Recipes & Replay](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs/recipes): Declarative execution pipelines for deterministic automation.
- [CLI Reference](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs/cli): `bitpeek` command-line syntax, JSON output piping, and exit codes.
- [MCP Server](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs/mcp): Local stdio server implementation and security sandbox model.
- [Limits & Guarantees](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs/limits): Resource bounds, memory constraints, and browser capabilities.
- [Privacy Model](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/docs/privacy): Strict local-first privacy boundary and zero-upload guarantee.
- [Replayable Examples](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/examples): 4 core technical demonstrations with verifiable input and output.
- [Performance Benchmarks](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/benchmarks): Measured latency, memory usage, and throughput across file sizes.
- [About & Upstream Contributions](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/about): Background on Yudis-bit's upstream contributions in LLVM, Vulkan, secp256k1, OpenSBI, MsQuic, and Kafel.
- [Changelog](https://bitpeek-seven.vercel.app/changelog): Detailed version history and feature roadmap.

## Tool Usage for AI Agents
Agents interacting with local files should run the local MCP stdio server or invoke the `bitpeek` CLI:
```sh
bitpeek inspect <file> --offset <n> --length <n> --type <t> --endian <le|be> --json
bitpeek find <file> --hex "<pattern>" --limit 100 --json
bitpeek strings <file> --min-length 4 --json
bitpeek hash <file> --algorithm sha256 --json
bitpeek structure <file> --format <elf|png> --json
bitpeek diff <reference> <current> --json
bitpeek patch verify <patch.json> --source <reference> --json
bitpeek recipe run <recipe.json> --input id=<file> --dry-run --json
```
